bull.b: Milestone ended Q1 with roughly $184M, boosted by a $75M RTW payment and net ATM/warrant proceeds. That funded runway into H2 2027 materially reduces near-term refinancing pressure, enabling continued commercial rollout and Phase III execution without immediate capital raises.

Securing Express Scripts formulary coverage (~25% commercial lives) represents durable payer validation that materially improves patient access and reimbursement prospects, a structural enabler for prescription growth and refill economics as the launch scales across additional PBMs and plans.

bull.t: High gross margin & improving TTM revenue
bull.b: Trailing revenue growth alongside a ~96% gross margin suggests the business can convert incremental sales to cash efficiently. If commercial adoption expands, the inherently high product margin supports long-term profitability potential once fixed launch and R&D costs normalize.

bear.b: The company generates materially negative operating and free cash flow (~- $51M TTM) and reported ~ $23.7M Q1 operating burn. Persistent negative cash flow makes the business reliant on external financing unless revenue ramps meaningfully, raising dilution and execution risk over the medium term.

bear.t: High leverage for a loss-making biotech
bear.b: Debt-to-equity near ~3.8x with ongoing losses constrains financial flexibility and increases refinancing and covenant risk. For a company still scaling revenue, the high leverage raises the probability of dilutive financings or restrictive debt terms that could hamper strategic optionality.

bear.t: Very limited product revenue & nascent refill depth
bear.b: Early commercial metrics show extremely limited sales (Q1 product revenue ~$0.2M) and most prescribers have written only one script, implying weak early repeat usage. Without sustained refill dynamics and broader payer/Medicare coverage, converting prescriptions into durable revenue is uncertain.
